description: We’re taking on the terrestrial analog challenge: using open NASA, ISRO and ESA Earth, Moon and Mars datasets to find and characterize new analog sites for lunar and Martian bases. Our plan is to score candidate regions (deserts, polar areas, volcanic terrain, caves) on topography, geology, thermal behavior and resources, then present the results as an interactive map and ranking tool.
summary:
We, Team 404-Coders have developed a visualization tool that shows the analogy between the Ecosystem of Mars and Earth using Sample Patches of both the planets. We have designed using a machine learning Pipeline which identifies and quantifies Planetary Analogs betweeen Mars and Earth by Extracting spatial patches, cross-analyze with an established Martian Dataset and Evaluate similarities using a 10 criteria framework obtained from the datasets to deliver precise planetary analog mappings. We have also done extensive research using data and discovered 2 new dimensions for comparing analog sites: Electro-magnetization and Electrostatic physics.
It addresses the challenge by automating the search for Earth locations that were previously unrecognized and which share the critical geological, topographical and environmental conditions with mars.
It is important because analog sites are usually poorly characterized, so this tool will help mission teams to test equipments and exploration strategies reliably before launching them for missions.
details:
Our Project

Our Project is an interactive visualization tool powered by a machine learning pipeline and open-source datasets, which systematically identifies and quantifies planetary analogs between Mars and Earth. It extracts spatial patches, cross-analyzes with Martian reference data and compares similarities using 10 different dimensions.

When a user inputs data (Earth) on our tool, it is verified with Martian data. The datasets are sent directly to the ML Pipeline which works under the KNN Model(which basically compares 10 earth terrain patches with 3624 Martian terrain patches, calculates distances and sorts to select top 5 nearest or shortest distances) and it uses JobLib for rendering and processing. Evaluating both the datasets gives relative analog similarities and their percentiles. After that, the ML Model visualizes the data directly based on the dimensions. It performs Earth and Mars DEM Data Processing. We connect the end points of the ML Pipeline and User Interface using APIs. The APIs display the results on UI, shows similarities in percentile and gives model performance based on 10 priority rankings. It also has a map explorer section which gives the representation and comparison data from the ml model.

Our team has also used research material and complex analysis to discover 2 new dimensions for comparing Analog sites: Electro-magnetization and Electrostatic physics(Di-electric constant). These new dimensions have been integrated into our ML model and have been tested for comparisons. Our test model has evaluated Electromagnetic interference using SHARAD Dataset.

Benefits

Our Project makes it faster and easier to find analogs on Earth which resemble the Mars Environment. Instead of choosing test sites by guessing, researchers will get a direct data-driven comparison. The KNN Model matches the terrain of Earth with 3264 Martian terrain patches using 10 dimensions and sorts the 5 closest matches. Scientists can test their rovers and landing systems on Earth in a cheaper and safer manner. Students and space enthusiasts can easily learn the planetal comparisons. In the long run, this project supports safer and better planned exploration around Earth.

Tools, coding lang, hardware/software

Research : Published Research Papers/conference papers, analysis done manually

ML Pipeline : The programming language used is Python. Tools used for ML are Scikit-learn, KNN, XGBoost (experimental classifier). Model Storage is using Joblib. Data sources used are NASA PDS, Mars Orbital Data Explorer, Planetary DEM Datasets. Hardware used is processor Intel Core i9-14900HX with Graphics NVDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU. Software used is Python 3.13 for model development and data processing.

APIs : FastAPI

Front End : React with Typescript builds pages and components of our web app. Vite (or Next.js) runs and bundles frontend. Tailwind CSS Styling. React Router moves between pages. TanStack Query fetches backend data and handles loading,caching and polling for job status. Leaflet used for interactive maps. Recharts Charts shows radar charts. Lucide-react Icon sets used. Inter and JetBrains Mono for text, numbers and coordinates. OpenAPI-typescript generates frontend types from backend's api description so the 2 stay in sync.

Creativity

Our team has done research and analysis to discover sites on Earth similar to Martian landscapes. Our Findings suggest the following places in Kazakhstan:

Rust-Red Minerology - Both Mars and red-rock formations in Bokty Mountain, Kyzylkup and Charyn canyon get their red and ochre hues from iron oxides (hematite) coating the sand and clay grains.

Bleached Halos (Microbial fingerprints) are found in Mangystau's red rocks as well as the Jezero crater in Mars.

Dried Marine Basins - Mangystau region containing evaporated layers of sedimentary rock, chalk and salt flats (Sor Tuzbair) previously belonging to Tethys Ocean. Similarity found in Mars's Jezero Crater.

Spherical concretions (Martian Blueberries) and Groundwater Mineralization found in Torysh.

Hyper-Arid wind and water Erosion along with Fluvial to Aeolian Transition found in Charyn and Bozzhyra, similar to Martian valleys.

Our Project is not just a visualization tool, it delivers a data-driven way to discover potential planetary analog locations.

Factors considered

We considered several factors important for future mars and moon operations such as Terrain Characteristics, Geological features, Surface conditions, Environmental differences and close resemblance with selected planetary regions.

We also considered the accurate analysis of the datasets and Machine Learning comparisons and presenting the information in a simpler and understandable way.

We have considered that Earth cannot perfectly reproduce certain conditions on moon and mars , so we focused more on identifying meaningful similarities , along with aknowledging the differences and limitations of each location.
